    • isWhitespace

      public static boolean isWhitespace(char charCode)
      Determines if the specified Character is a whitespace under the active WhitespaceMode: the Unicode White_Space property by default, or, when the "opennlp.whitespace.mode" system property selects WhitespaceMode.LEGACY, the union of Character.isWhitespace(int) and the Unicode Zs category (Character.SPACE_SEPARATOR) that OpenNLP 1.x and 2.x used.

      Tokenization, corpus format parsing, and feature generation all resolve whitespace through this method, so they share one WhitespaceMode for the life of the process; use isUnicodeWhitespace(char) directly where the Unicode definition should apply unconditionally, such as user-text normalization with no trained-model dependency.

      Parameters:
      charCode - The character to check.
      Returns:
      true if charCode represents a white space under the active WhitespaceMode, false otherwise.

    • split

      public static String[] split(CharSequence input, char separator)
      Splits input around literal occurrences of separator, with the same result as String.split(String) called with the single-character pattern Character.toString(separator) and a limit of 0: leading and middle empty fields are kept, trailing empty fields are removed, and empty input yields an array containing one empty string. The scan compares characters, so separator is always treated as a literal, including when it is a regular-expression metacharacter such as '.', '$' or '|', and supplementary code points in the input pass through untouched.
      Parameters:
      input - The text to split. Must not be null.
      separator - The literal field separator. Must not be a surrogate.
      Returns:
      The fields in order.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If input is null or separator is a surrogate.

    • split

      public static String[] split(CharSequence input, char separator, int limit)
      Splits input around literal occurrences of separator, with the same limit contract as String.split(String, int) applied to the single-character pattern Character.toString(separator): a positive limit applies at most limit - 1 splits and keeps trailing empty fields; 0 applies unlimited splits and removes trailing empty fields, exactly like split(CharSequence, char); a negative limit applies unlimited splits and keeps trailing empty fields. Empty input yields an array containing one empty string at every limit. The scan compares characters, so separator is always treated as a literal, including when it is a regular-expression metacharacter, and supplementary code points in the input pass through untouched.
      Parameters:
      input - The text to split. Must not be null.
      separator - The literal field separator. Must not be a surrogate, so that a supplementary code point in input is never split in half.
      limit - The maximum number of fields, or 0 for the default behavior, or negative for no limit.
      Returns:
      The fields in order.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If input is null or separator is a surrogate.

    • stripByteOrderMark

      public static String stripByteOrderMark(String input)
      Removes one leading byte order mark, U+FEFF, from input. A U+FEFF anywhere else is left in place, since there it is a zero width no-break space and part of the text.
      Parameters:
      input - The text to strip. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      input without its leading byte order mark, or input itself if it has none.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If input is null.

    • splitNonEmpty

      public static String[] splitNonEmpty(CharSequence input, char... separators)
      Splits input around literal occurrences of any of the separators and drops the empty fields that leading, trailing or adjacent separators would produce, so a run of separators acts as one and input made only of separators yields an empty array. The scan compares characters, so every separator is a literal, including a regular-expression metacharacter, and supplementary code points in the input pass through untouched.
      Parameters:
      input - The text to split. Must not be null.
      separators - The literal field separators. Must not be null or empty, and must not contain a surrogate.
      Returns:
      The non-empty fields in order.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If input or separators is null, separators is empty, or a separator is a surrogate.

    • isLineTerminator

      public static boolean isLineTerminator(int codePoint)
      Tests for a line terminator: line feed U+000A, carriage return U+000D, next line U+0085, line separator U+2028, or paragraph separator U+2029. This is the set Pattern treats as line terminators outside UNIX_LINES mode. It is narrower than UnicodeWhitespace.lineBreakCodePointSet(), which also holds vertical tab U+000B and form feed U+000C.
      Parameters:
      codePoint - The code point to test.
      Returns:
      true if codePoint ends a line.

    • isUnpairedSurrogate

      public static boolean isUnpairedSurrogate(int codePoint)
      Checks whether a code point taken from a CharSequence is a lone surrogate, U+D800 to U+DFFF, rather than a character. String.codePoints() and Character.codePointAt(CharSequence, int) return a surrogate only when it is not part of a valid high and low surrogate pair.
      Parameters:
      codePoint - The code point to test.
      Returns:
      true if codePoint is in the surrogate range.

    • isBlank

      public static boolean isBlank(CharSequence theString)
      Determines whether a CharSequence is blank: empty, or made up entirely of code points that isWhitespace(int) accepts. Unlike String.isBlank(), this follows the toolkit's whitespace definition, which includes the no-break spaces the JDK predicate leaves out, so a value spelled entirely from them cannot pass a blank check as content. Unlike isUnicodeBlank(CharSequence), it resolves through the active WhitespaceMode and does not treat null as blank.
      Parameters:
      theString - The CharSequence to examine. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      true if theString is empty or all whitespace.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if theString is null.

    • levenshteinDistance

      public static int[][] levenshteinDistance(String wordForm, String lemma)
      Computes the Levenshtein distance of two strings in a matrix.

      Based on this pseudo-code which in turn is based on the paper Wagner, Robert A.; Fischer, Michael J. (1974), "The String-to-String Correction Problem", Journal of the ACM 21 (1): 168-173

      Parameters:
      wordForm - The form as input.
      lemma - The target lemma.
      Returns:
      A 2-dimensional Levenshtein distance matrix.
